sections.h2: What the Richmond County Register of Deeds does
sections.html:
The office in Rockingham holds the deeds, deeds of trust, plats, marriage records and birth and death certificates for Richmond County, and it records new ones as they come in. When you sell, it is the stop where your deed to the buyer joins the permanent record.

Everything on file is public. A buyer, a title examiner or a curious neighbor can all ask for copies by paying the usual fees, so assume any deed you sign will be read by others.

The date of recording is what counts, because G.S. 47-18 ranks a deed against lien holders and later purchasers by when it was registered, not when it was signed.

Walk into 114 E. Franklin Street, Room 101, Rockingham, NC 28379. That is both the physical and mailing address, and the phone line is 910-997-8250.

Hours differ by service, so read the table before choosing a delivery time. Papers presented after 4:30 pm are recorded first on the following day.

If your closing runs late, ask whether your attorney's firm sends documents electronically, since that channel shuts half an hour sooner.

A deed through page 15 is $26 and each added page is $4, matching the statewide table in G.S. 161-10.

  • A mortgage or deed of trust has a bigger base, $64 for 35 pages.
  • Recording a payoff cancellation costs nothing.
  • Survey plats are $21 a sheet.
  • A certified copy begins at $5, with $2 per added page.

Over the counter, an uncertified copy of a deed or plat is 35 cents. To get one by mail, send your name and the approximate year the property was acquired.

sections.h2: Excise tax on a Richmond County deed
sections.html:
Sellers settle this tax when the deed is filed. The rate is a dollar per $500 of value, with a partial $500 rounded up, and G.S. 105-228.30 puts the payment ahead of recording.

Half stays in Richmond County's general fund, and half is passed up to Raleigh. Look for the line on your settlement statement and check it against the contract price.

sections.h2: Fixing the names on a deed
sections.html:
The staff will record a corrected deed but will not draft it. The fix is a fresh deed that an attorney drafts, the owner signs, a notary acknowledges and the office then records.

Situations where this comes up before a sale include:

  • A spouse added or removed after a marriage or divorce.
  • An heir who needs to appear on title after a death.
  • Co-owners who want to sell to one buyer together.

Each case needs the right signatures on the new deed, and signatures take time to gather. Settle it early so the closing date holds. Once the corrected deed is signed and notarized, bring it to the Rockingham counter with the recording fee, and ask your attorney to confirm which names must appear on the sale deed.

sections.h2: Deed and plat copies and notary oaths
sections.html:
For a copy, give staff your name and about when you acquired the land, in person or by mail. A plat can be requested as long as it was surveyed and recorded.

Notary oaths need no appointment. Any staff member can administer one during office hours.

Because the whole file is public, you can also look up your own mortgage cancellation after a payoff to confirm that the lien came off.

sections.h2: Other papers filed with a Richmond County sale
sections.html:
A deed is rarely the only paper. Under G.S. 47-18, an option, a contract to sell, a long lease (over three years) or a right of first refusal takes effect against outsiders only once registered, in order of time.

  • Owner-financed sales under Chapter 47H need the contract, or a memorandum of it, on record inside five business days.
  • A buyer's mortgage is filed as a deed of trust.
  • Surveys come in as plats.

Ask your attorney to list each document that will be filed, so none is held back. Each one is recorded in the order it arrives, so the deed to the buyer should go in before the buyer's deed of trust.

These go through the Richmond clerk of superior court instead. In a power-of-sale case the clerk holds the hearing, and notice must be served 10 or more days beforehand (G.S. 45-21.16).

Once a foreclosure sale is reported, anyone can submit an upset bid during the next ten days. It needs to beat the last figure by 5 percent and at least $750, and every new bid starts the ten days over.

For a modest estate, an affidavit can replace full administration when personal property net of liens stays at $20,000 or under. The deed that follows is recorded in Rockingham.

sections.h2: Questions to ask the Rockingham office before closing
sections.html:
A short call to 910-997-8250 can head off delays. The staff are used to questions from attorneys, title searchers and owners, and everything they hold is public.

  • Has the deed been indexed yet, and what book and page does it carry?
  • Did the cancellation of my old deed of trust record?
  • What is the total of fees for the page count of my filing?
  • Can my attorney's e-Recording submission still go in before the deadline?

Write down the answers with the date and the name of the person who gave them. Staff cannot interpret a document, but they can confirm what has been recorded and when.

sections.h2: Before recording, what a Richmond County seller should do
sections.html:
Get from the closing attorney the day the deed should be recorded and proof that your old loan was cancelled. After closing, search the county records for both and keep the recorded copies.

Property tax becomes a lien on the listing date, so the current bill stays with the parcel until paid. Ask the Richmond County tax office for the balance. Fees and excise tax are paid at the filing, and the return address you give should be one where the recorded original will reach you.

A cash buyer can shorten the wait for loan approval. The recording steps do not change: the deed still goes to Rockingham before 4:30, and your payoff and tax balance still come from the closing proceeds.

faqs.q: What hours does the Richmond County Register of Deeds record documents?
faqs.a: Staff remain until 5:00 PM, yet counter recording ends half an hour sooner and electronic filing ends at 4:00. Papers that come after 4:30 are recorded first the next morning, so a late closing can push your recording date back.

faqs.q: Where is the Richmond County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: At 114 E. Franklin Street, Room 101, Rockingham, NC 28379, which is also its mailing address. Call 910-997-8250 during business hours with questions.

faqs.q: How much is a photocopy of a recorded deed in Rockingham?
faqs.a: 35 cents a copy when you ask in person. Certified copies are priced under the state table instead, starting at $5 for page one.

faqs.q: Do I need an appointment to record a deed in Richmond County?
faqs.a: No appointment is required. Bring the signed, notarized deed during recording hours, or have an eligible submitter e-record it before 4:00 PM.

faqs.q: Can staff draft my deed for me?
faqs.a: No. An attorney or the owner has to prepare the deed, and it must be signed and notarized before it is brought in. The office records the paper and gives no advice on its wording.
